Photoinduced double [2 + 2] cycloaddition relay of
yne–allenones for highly diastereoselective
synthesis of hexacyclic 1-naphthols †
Shan-Shan Zhu, Jiang-Nan Zhou, Quan-Long Wu, Wen-Juan Hao,*
Shu-Jiang Tu
 and Bo Jiang
 *
A new photoinduced photocatalyst-free energy-transfer strategy for double [2 + 2] cycloaddition relay of
yne–allenones is reported for the ﬁrst time and used to produce a series of hitherto unreported hexacyc-
lic 1-naphthols with good yields and complete diastereoselectivity. The reaction pathway generates a
class of complex three-dimensional structures with two all-carbon quaternary centers evolved from the
planar conjugated system through cleavage and recombination of the C –C triple bond of yne –allenones,
enabling the direct formation of four new rings in one step.
Introduction
Cycloaddition reactions driven by visible light have long
proven to be flourishing and powerful tools for the synthesis
of various cyclic architectures under mild conditions. 1 In
addition to the inherent characteristics of atom-economy, high
stereoselectivity and sustainability, such reactions can directly
construct intricate cyclic sca ﬀolds that are di ﬃcult to obtain
by thermal reactions. As one of the most fundamental photo-
induced cycloaddition reactions, [2 + 2] cycloaddition reactions
have been extensively applied to assemble numerous four-
membered cyclic molecules in recent years.
2 Generally, photo-
chemical [2 + 2] cycloadditions proceed through an energy-
transfer (EnT) process, and substantial elegant studies have
been published by many research groups. 3 For example, the
group of Yoon reported an impressive visible light catalytic
[2 + 2] cycloaddition of styrenes in the presence of an iridium
(III) polypyridyl complex (Scheme 1a). 4 Kwon’s group developed
an energy transfer approach to obtain bridged cyclobutanes
through iridium( III)-catalyzed intramodular crossed [2 + 2]
cycloaddition of dienones upon visible light irradiation
(Scheme 1b).
5 Despite these advances, most of these
approaches developed so far require the intervention of photo-
sensitizers including organic and metal photocatalysts, thus
causing a complex work-up process. Therefore, the develop-
ment of photoinduced EnT strategies for [2 + 2] cycloaddition
reactions by means of the photosensitivity of substrates
without additional photocatalysts is strongly encouraged and
promising but full of challenges.
Recently, our group and others have developed intra-
molecular [2 + 2] cycloadditions and their in situ transform-
ations starting from benzene-linked yne –allenones,
6 furnish-
ing skeletally diverse naphthalen-1-ol derivatives. In particular,
we recently established a new reaction mode of benzene-linked
yne–allenones with alkenes or terminal alkynes, namely a

process was supported by carrying out systematic theoretical calcu-
lations.6d In continuation of our research in the area of double
[2 + 2] cycloaddition relay, we became interested in developing
such transformations by continuously using yne–allenones as start-
ing materials under photocatalytic conditions. As we implemented
this concept, we found that the conjugated yne –allenones have
photoabsorbing property in the absorption band range of
400–450 nm (see Fig. 2 and 3); thus we questioned whether photo-
induced double [2 + 2] cycloaddition relay of yne –allenones
assisted by their own photosensitivity would work, resulting in a
direct, atom-economical entry to polycyclic architectures, thereby
avoiding the use of photocatalysts while greatly simplifying the
work-up process. To our delight, the photocatalyst-free cyclodimeri-
zation reaction proceeded smoothly through an EnT process under
blue LED irradiation, leading to the formation of the hitherto unre-
ported hexacyclic 1-naphthols in good yields, with the complete
control of stereo- and regiochemistry in which two adjacent all-car-
bonyl stereogenic centers were constructed (Scheme 1c).
Remarkably, the current photoinduced EnT strategy enabled C–C
triple-bond cleavage of yne –allenones to access unprecedented
pentaleno[1,2-a:6a,6-a′]dinaphthalen-11-ones with good substrate
scope and 100% atom utilization, oﬀering an extensively attractive
approach for assembling complex molecular scaﬀolds. Herein we
elaborate on this attractive photoinduced double [2 + 2] cyclo-
addition relay.
Results and discussion
At the outset of our investigation, yne –allenone 1a was chosen
as the model substrate and the reaction of 1a was conducted
in dry CH 3CN under 30 W blue LEDs and an argon atmo-
sphere at 30 °C for 15 h. As expected, the reaction proceeded
readily, cleanly a ﬀording the hexacyclic product 2a in 65%
yield (Table 1, entry 1). Then, other light sources such as white
light and green light were examined. White light could drive
this transformation, but its e ﬃciency was lower than that
under blue light (entry 2). However, green light proved to be
ineﬀective as the expected target was not observed (entry 3).
Subsequently, we carefully investigated the e ﬀect of the solvent
by employing di ﬀerent dry aprotic solvents including 1,4-
dioxane, acetone, tetrahydrofuran (THF), N,N-dimethyl-
formamide (DMF), toluene, and 1,2-dichloroethane (DCE)
(entries 4 –9). The results revealed that these attempts did not
show any improvement on the obtainable yield. Elevating the
reaction temperature to 40 °C made the reaction system
chaotic, lowering the yield of 2a to 60% (entry 10). An incom-
plete consumption of 1a was detected and thus a significantly
reduced yield of 2a (30%) was provided when the reaction
temperature was 25 °C (entry 11). The reaction did not work
and the starting material 1a was recovered with the removal of
light irradiation (entry 12). A significant drop in the yield of 2a
was observed when the reaction was carried out under air con-
ditions, showing that O
2 is not beneficial for this photo-
induced cyclodimerization (entry 13).
Having demonstrated the viability of using the yne –alle-
none 1a in the photoinduced double [2 + 2] cycloaddition relay
(Table 1, entry 1), we set out to systematically investigate the
substrate scope of this protocol. The results are summarized
in Scheme 2. Initially, the influence of substituents (R 1) in the

1b–1c, ethyl 1d, tert-butyl 1e, methoxy 1f (PMP = p-methoxy-
phenyl)) and electron-withdrawing ( e.g. fluoro 1g, chloro 1h
and bromo 1i) groups at di ﬀerent positions on the phenyl ring
were compatible with these photocatalytic conditions,
enabling a C –C triple-bond cleavage process to furnish pro-
ducts 2b–2i in 45 –80% yields with complete diastereo-
selectivity. The presence of electron-withdrawing groups
seemed to decrease the e ﬃciency of the reaction as shown for
2g and 2h, in which moderate yields were obtained for both.
Notably, a thienyl-substituted counterpart 1j was found to
show a high reactivity profile, thus delivering the corres-
ponding product 2j as a single diastereoisomer in 70% yield.
Subsequently, the electronic nature of substituents (R
2) on the
internal aryl ring of substrates 1 was briefly investigated.
Several representative functional groups such as methyl
(1k–1m), fluoro ( 1n–1q) and chloro ( 1r–1w) were independently
installed at the C4 or C5 position of the internal arene ring
and these substrates ( 1k–1w) were then subjected to the stan-
dard conditions. As anticipated, these functional groups
oriented the complete diastereoselectivity to access the corres-
ponding products 2k–2w with comparable e ﬃciency. However,
cyclohexenyl substituted yne –allenone 1x seems reluctant to
undergo this reaction process as product 2x was detected in a
trace amount and could not be isolated. The results have been
shown in Scheme 2. This protocol represents a first example of
photoinduced [2 + 2] cycloaddition relay enabled C –C triple
bond cleavage for the highly diastereoselective synthesis of
complex three-dimensional architectures containing an unpre-
cedented polycyclic 1-naphthol unit and opens new avenues
for the development of photocatalyst-free photochemistry. The
structures of these products were fully characterized by NMR
spectroscopy and HRMS data (see the ESI †). The stereo-struc-
ture of 2q was identified by single-crystal X-ray di ﬀraction
(Fig. 1).
The practical utility of this photoinduced cyclodimerization
protocol was demonstrated by a scale-up experiment
(Scheme 3a). When carrying out the reaction at a 2 mmol
scale, the desired product 2q was delivered smoothly in 54%
yield. The experimental results showed the potential appli-
cation of this strategy in actual synthesis. The presence of con-
jugated α,β,γ,δ-unsaturated cycloketones provides the great
possibility of further modification of these hexacycles as these
molecules are good 1,6-eletrophilic acceptors. For instance,
treatment of 2q with dimethoxy(methyl)silane in the presence
of CuCN and 1,1 ′-bis(diphenylphosphino)ferrocene (DPPF)
ligand as a catalytic system cleanly a ﬀorded the reductive
product 3 in 68% yield under argon conditions (Scheme 3b).
7
To understand the mechanism of this reaction, 1.5 equiva-
lents of 2,2,6,6-tetramethyl-1-piperidinyloxy (TEMPO) or butyl-
hydroxytoluene (BHT) as a radical scavenger 8 were subjected to
the reaction with 1a under the standard conditions, and a
slightly reduced yield of product 2a was obtained (Scheme 4a),
indicating that the current photocatalysis may involve an EnT
process, rather than a radical pathway. Next, the conversion of
1a into 2a was significantly suppressed by the triplet quencher
2,5-dimethylhexa-2,4-diene (Scheme 4b),

Based on the experimental results and previous reports,
3a,10
a putative pathway leading to the formation of 2a is proposed
in Scheme 5. Initially, yne –allenone 1a rapidly undergoes an
intramolecular [2 + 2] cycloaddition to o ﬀer adduct intermedi-
ate A. Subsequently, under the irradiation of visible light, the
ground state A can reach the triplet state A* via energy transfer,
followed by their intermolecular [2 + 2] cycloaddition to give
the intermediate B.
5 The ring-opening of the four-membered
carbocycle, because of its ring tension, easily occurs under
visible light irradiation, giving the eight-membered ring inter-
mediate C, which undergoes isomerization and cycloaddition
under irradiation of visible light to yield the zwitterion inter-
mediate E. Subsequent isomerization and proton transfer (PT)
give the final product 2a. Although the detailed mechanism
for this cyclodimerization is not clear to us yet, the current
observations o ﬀer a potential and attractive pathway for the
construction of complex three-dimensional architectures from
staring materials with a planar conjugated system.
Conclusions
In summary, starting from easily available yne –allenones, we
have established a photoinduced photocatalyst-free EnT strat-
egy for realizing double [2 + 2] cycloaddition relay, by which a
wide set of hitherto unreported hexacyclic 1-naphthols with
two adjacent all-carbonyl quaternary centers were e ﬃciently
synthesized in a high diastereoselective and atom-economical
fashion. The reaction process is considered to proceed
through a double [2 + 2] cycloaddition relay, C –C triple bond
cleavage and hydrogen atom transfer sequence. The photo-
catalysis enjoys the complete control of regio- and diastereo-
chemistry, good compatibility with di ﬀerent types of sub-
stituents and mild reaction conditions as well as 100% atom
utilization and high annulation e ﬃciency (formation of up to
four new rings). Further investigations regarding the mecha-
nism as well as synthetic application are underway in our
laboratory.
